limits: Known prior outcome exposure; descriptive/estimative, not confirmatory. Intervals condition on fixed training/design; no multiplicity adjustment.
N3 balanced contains a fixed three-emotion subset; primary single averages all feasible emotions. Class-matched secondary is separately retained.
Most naive N3 loss also appears under balanced references. These data do not isolate emotion skew as the main cause or distinguish mean-estimation from variance-estimation mechanisms.
E0 uses globally standardized training and queries; E1..E4 use the separately fitted speaker-normalized Ridge pipeline. Their difference is a pipeline comparison, not a fixed-weight intervention.
Rescue over naive E1 is not evidence of beating the global-standardization baseline. Derived estimator-vs-global point estimates have no new interval.
Harm share thresholds each speaker after averaging draws, repeated splits and reference emotions. It does not mean every trial or every utterance is harmed.
RAVDESS N3 single excludes neutral; N5 single feasible only in CREMA-D. Do not merge differing class sets/corpora into a single common effect.
oracle_all uses query features, is non-deployable and not a guaranteed upper bound; no real-call/online risk or optimization claim.
